waivers.reason: Reviewed 2026-10-10 against RustSec database 7eebec69c352c7191b1f13eb95dd510eeca5d1de for the frozen public-testnet maintenance baseline b819911dbf. This is an unmaintained-package advisory with no patched version, not a disclosed parser vulnerability. Native P2P frames use bounded HNW1/postcard; bincode remains in persisted metadata, wallet files, and proof artifact decoding, including peer-supplied proof bytes. Replacing those encodings would change compatibility and exceeds this maintenance release. Accept only that existing maintenance risk through 2026-10-24; this is not a production-security acceptance or a claim that all bincode parsing is safe.
waivers.remediation: DEP-2026-0002: by 2026-10-24, review versioned canonical codec migration for persisted metadata, wallet files, and proof artifacts with byte-format and adversarial decode compatibility evidence; remove bincode 1.3.3 or explicitly re-review the unresolved maintenance risk before further releases.

waivers.reason: Reviewed 2026-10-10 against RustSec database 7eebec69c352c7191b1f13eb95dd510eeca5d1de. waivers.reason: Reviewed 2026-10-10 against RustSec database 7eebec69c352c7191b1f13eb95dd510eeca5d1de and the checksum-verified reed-solomon-erasure 6.0.0 crate. The only locked lru 0.7.8 consumer is reed-solomon-erasure in state-da. Hegemon constructs ReedSolomon and calls encode, never reconstruct; upstream cache use is confined to reconstruction via get/put, not LruCache::pop. Its key type is Vec<usize>, with no panicking custom key destructor. The reported use-after-free requires pop, a panicking key Drop, and continued cache use after caught unwinding; those preconditions are absent from this reviewed path. Retain only this fixed call/type graph through 2026-10-24; changes to reconstruction, cache keys, or lru use invalidate this waiver.
waivers.remediation: DEP-2026-0007: by 2026-10-24, review and test a reed-solomon-erasure upgrade or replacement whose dependency graph removes lru 0.7.8 or uses lru >=0.18.2, with unchanged DA encoding commitments and allocation limits; further retention needs a fresh path review.
